# crosswork_health_settings (Data Source)

This data source can read the health settings of the performance monitoring dashboards.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "crosswork_health_settings" "example" {
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `instance` (String) Select an instance of the provider configuration by its name. Leave it unset to use the default instance.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id of the object
- `rows` (Attributes Map) Health settings by metric key, for example `CPU_cpuUtilization`. Only editable metrics can be changed. A metric that is not listed keeps its categories (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows))

<a id="nestedatt--rows"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows`

Read-Only:

- `categories` (Attributes List) Levels of the metric. A range level has `min` and `max`, either may be left out; a level of a metric with values has `values` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows--categories))
- `unit` (String) Unit of the metric, for a metric that offers several (`bps`, `kbps`, `mbps` or `gbps` for the post-FEC BER). Leave it out to keep the unit

<a id="nestedatt--rows--categories"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows.categories`

Read-Only:

- `level` (String) Severity of the level
- `max` (Number) Upper end of a range level
- `min` (Number) Lower end of a range level
- `values` (List of Number) Whole numbers of a level of a metric that lists values, such as the clock state
